title: Exercise a real noncanonical Windows spelling in the refusal-path test
outcome: Replace the inert dot alias in the task-sync refusal fixture with a case alias that survives path construction, and check omission of both caller and admitted paths from JSON.
acceptance: The Windows fixture passes a spelling that differs from the admitted plain checkout and asserts that difference.
The test checks human stderr against the admitted checkout, includes stderr on failure, and omits both caller and admitted paths from structured JSON.
The corrected case passes on Windows and the same test passes on Linux and macOS after a fresh candidate is cut onto current master.
